title: Aspartame and cancer - new evidence for causation.
ehr_evidence: The manuscript is a commentary reanalyzing Ramazzini Institute rodent carcinogenicity bioassays; the underlying data source was tissue from Sprague-Dawley rats and Swiss mice analyzed by immunohistochemistry and morphological reclassification, not electronic health records.
summary: A commentary reanalyzing Ramazzini Institute rodent carcinogenicity bioassays of aspartame, finding that immunohistochemical and morphological re-evaluation confirmed aspartame causes dose-related hematolymphatic malignancies in rats and mice.
key_findings: Reanalysis confirmed 72 (92.3%) of 78 lesions originally diagnosed as hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue tumors (HLTs) were malignant, with 3 (3.8%) premalignant and 3 reclassified as chronic inflammation with fibrosis.

Statistically significant increase in incidence of all hematolymphatic malignancies (p=0.006), including significant increases in lymphomas (p=0.032) and leukemias (p=0.031) in rodents exposed to aspartame.
No histological evidence of infection caused by Mycoplasma pulmonis or other microorganisms.
captured_features: immunohistochemical markers (Ki67, CD3, PAX5, CD20, CD68, TdT, CD45, CD14, CD33)
hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue tumor incidence and dose-response
study_design: Commentary/review reanalyzing prior rodent carcinogenicity bioassays (chronic toxicology/carcinogenesis study)
population: Rodents: Sprague-Dawley rats and Swiss mice (2270 rats, 852 mice)
exposure_domain: Aspartame (artificial sweetener), dietary exposure including prenatal
limitations: Commentary based on animal (rodent) data, not human epidemiological studies
Relies on reanalysis of a single institute's (Ramazzini Institute) bioassays
No direct human cancer incidence data analyzed
